rulings.Case Title: BLUE ROOFING COMPANY VS. CITY GARDENS 333,LLC
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion For Protective Order
rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Tuesday, July 21, 2026, Line 1, REAL PARTY IN INTEREST CITYSPACES 333, LLC's Motion For Protective Order. 2 - Nonparty CitySpaces 333, LLC's motion for protective order is denied without prejudice. In a companion order, the court has denied Blue's Roofing's motion to compel further responses to requests for production and interrogatories served on judgment debtor City Gardens 333, LLC. In light of that ruling, there is no basis at this time to enter a protective order. To the extent CitySpaces 333 seeks protection against future discovery efforts by Blue's Roofing, it must meet and confer in advance of filing its motion. The court encourages Blue's Roofing and CitySpaces to negotiate an appropriate protective order to manage CitySpaces's confidentiality concerns. The court observes that there is authority for CitySpaces 333 to seek a protective order, notwithstanding that it is not a party, because it is a person affected by the discovery. (Code Civ. Proc., sec. 2017.020, subd. (a) ["The court may make this determination pursuant to a motion for protective order by a party or other affected person."].) For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 301 Zoom ID 161 502 4290; Passcode 700956.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept301tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing. Counsel for the prevailing party is required to prepare a proposed order which repeats verbatim the substantive portion of the tentative ruling and must email it to contestdept301tr@sftc.org prior to the hearing even if the tentative ruling is not contested. The court no longer provides a court reporter in the Law & Motion or Discovery Department. Parties may retain their own reporter, who may appear in the courtroom or remotely. A retained reporter must be a California certified court reporter (CSR), for only a CSR's transcript may be used in California courts. If a CSR is being retained, include in your email all of the following: their name, CSR and telephone numbers, and their individual work email address. =(301/CVA).

rulings.Calendar Matter: Amended MOTION TO QUASH SERVICE OF SUMMONS OR STAY OR DISMISS
rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Tuesday, July 21, 2026, Line 12, DEFENDANT ROCKWOOD CAPITAL, LLC, HARRISON STREET REAL ESTATE CAPITAL LLC, MATTHEW FRIEDMAN's Amended MOTION TO QUASH SERVICE OF SUMMONS OR STAY OR DISMISS. 1 - Defendant Matthew Friedman's motion to quash is denied as unripe. Friedman has not been served. A motion to quash service of summons lies where a summons has been served. (Code Civ. Proc., sec. 418.10, subd. (a)(1).) Because Friedman has not yet been served, there is nothing for the court to decide. No one disputes that the court may not exercise personal jurisdiction over him before he has been served or has voluntarily appeared in the case, but he does not show any attempt to exercise personal jurisdiction over him prior to service.
